chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from ‘Ali ibn Ri’ab, from Durays al-Kunasi, from Abi Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said:

No remission is granted in the hudud that belong to Allah apart from the Imam. But as for what pertains to the rights of people within a hadd, there is no objection to its being pardoned apart from the Imam.

key_terms.اَلْإِمَامِ: the Imam, the legitimate authority over such matters
key_terms.اَلْحُدُودِ: the prescribed legal punishments or penal limits
key_terms.حَدٍّ: a prescribed legal punishment in a specific case
key_terms.حُقُوقِ اَلنَّاسِ: the rights of people or private claims of individuals
key_terms.لِلَّهِ: belonging to Allah, meaning divine rights

ai.seo_question: Can hadd punishments be pardoned without the Imam in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith distinguishes between hudud connected to the rights of Allah and aspects tied to the rights of people. It states that divinely ordained penal limits are not to be waived independently of the Imam, while matters involving personal rights within such cases may be pardoned by those entitled to them.
